title: How cells reproduce (mitosis)
subtitle: One cell copies its DNA, then splits into two daughter cells that carry the same chromosomes.

stages.title: Interphase
stages.desc: The cell grows and copies its DNA: each chromosome becomes two sister chromatids.

stages.title: Prophase
stages.desc: Chromosomes coil up into visible X shapes and the spindle begins to form.

stages.title: Metaphase
stages.desc: Spindle fibers line the chromosomes up across the middle of the cell.

stages.title: Anaphase
stages.desc: The sister chromatids are pulled apart toward opposite ends of the cell.

stages.title: Telophase
stages.desc: A new nuclear envelope forms around each of the two sets of chromosomes.

stages.title: Cytokinesis
stages.desc: The cytoplasm pinches in two, leaving two identical daughter cells.

edges.cycle: each daughter cell can begin the cycle again at interphase

why.title: WHY IT MATTERS
why.body: Mitosis is how a body grows, replaces worn-out cells and heals wounds. When its checks fail, cells can divide out of control, as in cancer.

same.title: WHAT STAYS THE SAME
same.body: Each daughter cell gets a full copy of the DNA: the same chromosomes, in the same number, as the parent cell.
